title: Rabbi Shaul
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman reports that Yuḥasin states that he lived in the time of Rabbi Zeira, and [the author] wrote in Seder HaDorot: "I did not find [him]."
But in truth he is indeed [found] in the Jerusalem Talmud, Maaserot, ch. 3, halakha 2: "Rabbi Zeira asked — Rabbi Shaul said: sometimes it bursts."
He is likewise mentioned in [the Jerusalem Talmud,] Maaser Sheni, ch. 4, halakha 1: "Rabbi Shaʾil asked: consider for yourself, etc."
And in the old Midrash Shmuel: Rabbi Shaul in the name of Rabbi Betzalel.
At the beginning of Ruth Rabbah, chapter 1, Hyman reports the erroneous reading “Rabbi asked Rabbi Betzalel”; he proposes reading “Rabbi Shaul in the name of Rabbi Betzalel.”

notes.text: Shaul, Shail and the verb sha-al (“asked”) are retained in explaining Hyman’s proposed correction.
